title: Sensitive Data Exposure - Password Hash Exposure in GET /api/v1/users
description: The GET /api/v1/users endpoint in the vulnerable API returns a list of all users with their passwordHash field exposed in the response. The listUsers use case returns User entities which include the passwordHash field (Argon2id hash). The vulnerable handler directly serializes the User entities to JSON without filtering out the passwordHash field, exposing all users' password hashes in the list response.
impact: Full password hash exfiltration. An authenticated attacker can retrieve Argon2id password hashes for all users in the system via a single GET request to /api/v1/users. Argon2id hashes can be subjected to offline brute-force attacks (GPU: ~10k H/s per GPU). With a list of all users' hashes, an attacker can perform offline cracking at scale.
mitigation: 1) Explicitly exclude passwordHash from user response DTOs in both list and single user endpoints. 2) Use a UserResponseDTO that explicitly defines allowed fields (id, name, email, role, status, createdAt, updatedAt) and excludes passwordHash. 2) Implement a UserResponseMapper or UserSerializer that explicitly defines the public API shape. 4) Secure API (api-secure) explicitly excludes passwordHash in response mapping.

history.details: Initial audit finding recorded for passwordHash exposure in GET /users list
